body.statement: Let \(U\) and \(W\) be independent real-valued random variables.  If \(\mathbb E[(U+W)^2]<\infty\), then \(\mathbb E[U^2]<\infty\) and \(\mathbb E[W^2]<\infty\).
body.proof_tex:
Because \(W\) is real valued, the events \(\{|W|\le r\}\), \(r\in\mathbb N\), increase to the whole sample space.  Hence there is an \(R\in\mathbb N\) for which
\[
 p_R:=\Pr(|W|\le R)>0.
\]
On the event \(\{|U|>2R,\ |W|\le R\}\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
 |U+W|\ge |U|-|W|\ge |U|/2.
\]
All integrands below are nonnegative, so the inequalities remain valid even before integrability has been established.  Independence of \(U\) and \(W\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E[(U+W)^2]
 &\ge \mathbb E\!\left[(U+W)^2
       \mathbf 1_{\{|U|>2R\}}\mathbf 1_{\{|W|\le R\}}\right]\\
 &\ge \frac14\mathbb E\!\left[U^2
       \mathbf 1_{\{|U|>2R\}}\mathbf 1_{\{|W|\le R\}}\right]\\
 &=\frac{p_R}{4}\mathbb E\!\left[U^2
       \mathbf 1_{\{|U|>2R\}}\right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
The left side is finite and \(p_R>0\), so the last expectation is finite.  The complementary part is bounded by
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[U^2\mathbf 1_{\{|U|\le2R\}}\right]\le4R^2.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E[U^2]<\infty\).  Interchanging \(U\) and \(W\) proves \(\mathbb E[W^2]<\infty\).
